properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 28 at 11:39PM MST until September 29 at 6:45AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Paria River in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 645 AM MST /745 AM MDT/ Tonight.

* At 1139 PM MST /1239 AM MDT/, a river gauge on the Paria River in
Utah reported a rapid rise of 4.47 feet from heavy rain over the
Paria River. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Paria River.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Paria River.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Paria Canyon, Paria River Slot Canyon, Vermilion Cliffs National
Monument and Lees Ferry.

This includes the Colorado River near mile marker 0.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Lees Ferry Camp Site.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Colorado River and Paria River.
properties.instruction:
Get out of the Paria River slot canyon! Flood waters will flow down
the Paria River, reaching the confluence with the Colorado River at
Lees Ferry around 3-6 hours from initial issuance.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 6:45 AM MST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 6:45 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 28 at 11:57PM MDT until September 29 at 1:45AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
At 1157 PM MDT, local law enforcement reported heavy rain over the
Cottonwood Burn Scar in Piute County. Approximately 0.5 and 1 inch of
rain has fallen. Flash flooding is already occurring with flows
reported in City Creek. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will
result in water and debris moving through the City Creek, Tenmile
Creek, Gold Gulch, and Cottonwood Creek drainages. The debris flow
can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials. This
water and debris may impact portions of Highway 89 between Junction
and Marysvale.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing flash
flooding in and around the Cottonwood Burn Scar in Piute
County.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Cottonwood Burn Scar in Piute County.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Cottonwood Creek, Gold Gulch, Tenmile Creek, and City Creek near
Junction.

This includes US Route 89 between mile markers 164 and 175.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Cottonwood Burn Scar in Piute County. Severe debris flows can
also be anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed
away in places. If you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, roads and normally dry washes is likely. The heavy rains will
likely trigger debris flows in steep terrain, especially in and
around drainages such as City Creek, Tenmile Creek, Gold Gulch, and
Cottonwood Creek.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 28 at 11:42PM MDT until September 29 at 4:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
At 1142 PM MDT, trained weather spotters reported thunderstorms
producing heavy rain in upper headwaters of the Paria River
downstream to the Arizona border and Wahweap Creek to its terminus in
Lake Powell. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported a very large flood wave moving
down Wahweap Creek toward Lake Powell near the town of Big
Water.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, and slickrock areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
The Paria River downstream to the Arizona border and Wahweap Creek
downstream to Lake Powell.

This includes US Route 89 between mile markers 2 and 12...and between
mile markers 18 and 22.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain. Dry
washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 28 at 10:11PM PDT until September 29 at 12:00AM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
FFWVEF

The National Weather Service in Las Vegas has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Mohave County in northwestern Arizona...
San Bernardino County in southern California...
South Central Clark County in southern Nevada...

* Until midnight PDT /midnight MST/.

* At 1011 PM PDT /1011 PM MST/, Thunderstorm activity persists across
central Mohave County and the Mohave Valley into the overnight
hours. Widespread rainfall of 1 to 4 inches has resulted in pockets
of ongoing flooding and excessive runoff. Expect rainfall rates to
diminish over the next several hours; however the flood threat
still persists.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Searchlight, Cal-Nev-Ari, Highway 95 And I-40 and Essex.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 28 at 7:56PM MST until September 29 at 2:45AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Havasu Creek basin in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...This includes the
Colorado River between river miles 156 and 158.

* Until 245 AM MST Tuesday.

* At 756 PM MST, a river gauge on the Cataract Creek reported a rapid
rise of 5 feet from thunderstorms producing heavy rain over the
Havasu Creek basin. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Havasu Creek basin.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Havasu Creek basin.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Little Navajo Falls, Mooney Falls, Beaver Falls, Supai, Hualapai
Hilltop and Havasupai Reservation.

This includes the Colorado River between river miles 156 and 158.

This includes the following swimming holes...
All swimming holes on Havasu Creek near Supai.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Colorado River, Little Coyote Canyon, Pasture Wash and Havasu
Creek.
properties.instruction:
Campers and hikers should hustle to higher ground immediately! Stay
away from creeks and washes!

Foot bridges will be washed out in Supai Campground. Some campsites
will be flooded. Campers may be stranded in portions of the
campground.
